metadata.title: The Photoelectric Effect: Why Colour Beats Brightness (Worked Example)
metadata.thing: light packets hitting a metal plate; the photon energy E=hf compared against the work function phi, worked with real numbers for sodium (blue ejects, red never does)
metadata.color_notes: Plate/electrons/axes = ink #1a1a1a. Blue packet/eject = blue #2A6FB0. Red packet/the 'no-ejection' verdict + boxed answer = red #C0392B. The formula highlight = accent #5A5653. Math is MathTex (LaTeX); prose/labels are Shadows Into Light.
metadata.math_rendering: All formulas render as Manim MathTex (LaTeX, MacTeX). hc = 1240 eV*nm.

beats.narration_text:
Bear's Notes

The Photoelectric Effect: Why Colour Beats Brightness
beats.tts_normalized_text:
Bear's Notes.

The Photoelectric Effect: Why Colour Beats Brightness.
beats.new_visual_element: title card: brand + a plate-and-photon hero motif + title

beats.narration_text: A blinding red lamp frees no electrons — a faint blue one frees them instantly.
beats.tts_normalized_text: A blinding red lamp frees no electrons — a faint blue one frees them instantly.
beats.new_visual_element: narration card + red plate (nothing) vs blue plate (electron flies)

beats.narration_text: The trick is that light's energy arrives in fixed, colour-sized packets.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The trick is that light's energy arrives in fixed, colour-sized packets.
beats.new_visual_element: narration card + small red packet, big blue packet

beats.narration_text: Light comes in packets, and each packet carries an energy set by its colour.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Light comes in packets, and each packet carries an energy set by its colour.

beats.narration_text: Red packets are weak; blue packets are strong.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Red packets are weak; blue packets are strong.
beats.new_visual_element: short red energy bar, tall blue bar

beats.narration_text: Freeing an electron needs one packet that clears the metal's escape energy.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Freeing an electron needs one packet that clears the metal's escape energy.
beats.new_visual_element: escape-energy threshold line; blue clears it, red doesn't

beats.narration_text: Let's turn that into a formula.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Let's turn that into a formula.
beats.new_visual_element: plate on the left, space for math on the right

beats.narration_text: A packet's energy is E equals h f — or h c over lambda.
beats.tts_normalized_text: A packet's energy is E equals h f — or h c over lambda.

beats.narration_text: Freeing an electron costs a fixed amount — the work function, phi.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Freeing an electron costs a fixed amount — the work function, phi.
beats.new_visual_element: phi labelled as the escape cost

beats.narration_text: Whatever's left over becomes the electron's kinetic energy.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Whatever's left over becomes the electron's kinetic energy.

beats.narration_text: Below a threshold frequency, f-naught equals phi over h, nothing comes off at all.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Below a threshold frequency, f naught equals phi over h, nothing comes off at all.

beats.narration_text: Put numbers on it: sodium's work function is about two point two eight electron-volts.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Put numbers on it: sodium's work function is about two point two eight electron volts.
beats.new_visual_element: givens: sodium, phi = 2.28 eV; boxed formula at top

beats.narration_text: A blue photon at 450 nanometres carries about two point seven six electron-volts.
beats.tts_normalized_text: A blue photon at 450 nanometres carries about two point seven six electron volts.

beats.narration_text: Subtract the work function — about zero point four eight electron-volts of kinetic energy, and the electron flies.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Subtract the work function — about zero point four eight electron volts of kinetic energy, and the electron flies.

beats.narration_text: A red photon at 700 nanometres carries only about one point seven seven electron-volts.
beats.tts_normalized_text: A red photon at 700 nanometres carries only about one point seven seven electron volts.

beats.narration_text: That's below two point two eight — so no electron escapes, no matter how bright.
beats.tts_normalized_text: That's below two point two eight — so no electron escapes, no matter how bright.

beats.narration_text: The cutoff sits at lambda-naught equals h c over phi — about five hundred forty-four nanometres.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The cutoff sits at lambda naught equals h c over phi — about five hundred forty four nanometres.
beats.new_visual_element: threshold wavelength on a spectrum strip

beats.narration_text: Turning up the brightness only sends more packets — not more energy in each one.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Turning up the brightness only sends more packets — not more energy in each one.
beats.new_visual_element: many red packets, still no ejection

beats.narration_text: So a blinding red lamp stays useless, while a dim blue one works on the first hit.
beats.tts_normalized_text: So a blinding red lamp stays useless, while a dim blue one works on the first hit.

beats.narration_text: Explaining this is what forced light to be quantized — Einstein's 1905 photon.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Explaining this is what forced light to be quantized — Einstein's 1905 photon.

beats.narration_text: The whole story is one line — kinetic energy equals h f minus phi.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The whole story is one line — kinetic energy equals h f minus phi.

beats.narration_text: Colour sets the energy per hit; brightness only sets how many hits.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Colour sets the energy per hit; brightness only sets how many hits.
